name: ICCTG BCG
aliases: Interstitial Cystitis Clinical Trials Group BCG trial
registry: Interstitial Cystitis Clinical Trials Group protocol 2
question: Does intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin improve global symptoms more than placebo instillation in treatment-refractory interstitial cystitis?

design.population: Participants met NIDDK interstitial cystitis criteria and had at least moderate pain and urinary frequency for at least six months despite prior treatment.
design.locator: Mayer 2005 PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

verdictNote: Week-34 global response did not differ significantly from placebo.
takeaway: Six weekly intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin instillations yielded 21% week-34 global response versus 12% with placebo in treatment-refractory interstitial cystitis; the primary comparison did not meet statistical significance (P = 0.062).

reports.label: Randomized primary report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation, 2005 Apr; exact publication day not stated
reports.citation: Mayer R, Propert KJ, Peters KM, et al. "A randomized controlled trial of intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guerin for treatment refractory interstitial cystitis." *J Urol.* 2005;173(4):1186-1191. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000152337.82806.e8

results.measure: Patient-reported global response at week 34, with IC medication use at weeks 31–34
results.note: Responder counts and arm denominators were not stated in the primary abstract.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

harms.label: Overall adverse events
harms.note: A large number of events occurred with BCG; the abstract reports no statistically significant difference in overall adverse-event rates between groups, without counts.

delivery.label: Blinded intravesical treatment
delivery.value: Six weekly instillations of BCG or placebo.

delivery.label: Randomized study withdrawal
delivery.value: 17 of 265 randomized participants withdrew from the study.

reports.label: Open-label BCG after nonresponse
reports.citation: Propert KJ, Mayer R, Nickel JC, et al. "Did patients with interstitial cystitis who failed to respond to initial treatment with bacillus Calmette-Guerin or placebo in a randomized clinical trial benefit from a second course of open label bacillus Calmette-Guerin?" *J Urol.* 2007;178(3 Pt 1):886-890. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.05.052

results.measure: Patient-reported global response after an open-label BCG course in prior nonresponders
results.note: Both groups received BCG in this nonrandomized extension; group labels refer to original assignment. Group denominators were not reported in the abstract.

harms.label: Open-label course adverse events
harms.note: Most participants reported at least one event, mainly pain, genitourinary symptoms or gastrointestinal disturbances; no between-group difference was reported.

delivery.label: Open-label treatment
delivery.value: A six-week intravesical BCG course was offered to prior nonresponders; 156 elected it and 18 withdrew during the extension.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

reports.label: Extended responder follow-up
reports.citation: Propert KJ, Mayer R, Nickel JC, et al. "Followup of patients with interstitial cystitis responsive to treatment with intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guerin or placebo." *J Urol.* 2008;179(2):552-555. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.09.035
reports.followUp: 68 weeks after original randomization, among week-34 responders
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods and Results, Figure 1

results.measure: Moderate or marked improvement at week 68 among original week-34 responders enrolled in follow-up
results.note: Of 44 responders identified at clinical sites at week 34, 38 entered the observational follow-up; five withdrawals remain in the week-68 denominators.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph following Figure 1

delivery.label: Original instillation volume and retention
delivery.locator: Full text, Discussion, paragraph beginning 'It could be argued'
